content:
Using Descartes’ circle theorem for the three mutually tangent base circles:

\[
k_1=\frac16,\quad k_2=k_3=\frac1{24}
\]

For the fourth tangent circle:

\[
k_4 = k_1+k_2+k_3 \pm 2\sqrt{k_1k_2+k_2k_3+k_3k_1}
\]

\[
k_1+k_2+k_3 = \frac16+\frac1{24}+\frac1{24}=\frac14
\]

\[
k_1k_2+k_2k_3+k_3k_1
= \frac1{144}+\frac1{576}+\frac1{144}
= \frac1{64}
\]

\[
2\sqrt{\frac1{64}}=\frac14
\]

Thus

\[
k_4=\frac14 \pm \frac14
\]

The nonzero finite solution is \(k_4=\frac12\), so the radius is

\[
r=\frac1{k_4}=2
\]

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
